item.title: [6.9] The Target Is a Predicate: Predicate-State Grounding for Semantic-Level Video Reasoning Segmentation
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

In this paper, we introduce Predicate-State Video Reasoning Segmentation (PS-VRS), where a query defines a dynamic predicate $P(o,t)$ over objects and time rather than a fixed object identity. Existing methods typically treat the target as permanently active once identified, leading to over-emission of masks during vacant intervals and failure to handle target switching. To address this, we...

WHY IT MATTERS

Introduces a new benchmark and grounding pipeline for semantic-level video reasoning segmentation that improves over baselines by addressing temporal predicate states.

item.description:

Early successes on agentic robotics point to a potential paradigm shift toward using coding agents to control robots. item.title: [6.7] Reasoning-Aware Relational Representation Learning for Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation (OV-SGG) requires models to recognize visual relationships beyond the training vocabulary, yet existing methods often rely on dataset-specific object--predicate co-occurrence patterns. Under long-tailed distributions and noisy object localization, such reliance leads to biased, entangled relation representations, limiting both rare-relation recognition...

WHY IT MATTERS

The paper introduces a novel framework (RaRe) that leverages MLLM-generated chain-of-thought rationales directly for structured relation representation learning in open-vocabulary scene graph generation, addressing long-standing co-occurrence bias.
